newsitem.title: USA: Clorox to acquire Armor All.
newsitem.headline: Clorox to acquire Armor All.

text.p: Home cleaning giant Clorox Co said Tuesday it plans to acquire Armor All Products Corp in a deal valued at $400 million.
Clorox said it will tender for all of Armor All's common stock at $19.09 a share in a move aimed at establishing itself in the growing automotive cleaning products market.
Clorox which had fiscal 1996 earnings of $222 million on sales of $2.2 billion said the acquisition is expected to dilute earnings for fiscal 1997 by about two or three percent.

Armor All has approved the tender agreement and recommends that its stockholders accept the Clorox offer. McKesson Corp, which owns 55 percent of Armor All's common stock, has agreed to tender all of its shares and said it will record an after-tax gain of about $100 million from the sale.
Based in Orange County, Calif., Armor All, which makes automotive cleaning and proctective products had sales of $186 million in fiscal 1996.

"This acquisition is right on target with our strategy of finding strong equities in new categories close in to what we do and where we can add value," said Clorox Chairman Craig Sullivan. "Armor All is a great brand equity with leading positions in the market and extraordinarily high consumer awareness and satisfaction ratings."

Clorox said it will fund the acquisition with cash and short-term borrowings. The tender is expected to begin December 2 and close by the end of the year. Armor All's regular quarterly dividend of $0.16 a share will be paid on January 2 to stockholders of record December 2.

Shares of Clorox, which makes home cleaning products, bleaches, cat litter, sauces and insecticides closed 1/4 higher at 105-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange. Armor All shares ended unchanged at 17-1/2 on Nasdaq.
